newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican sends condolences over haj tragedy.
newsitem.headline: Vatican sends condolences over haj tragedy.

text.p: The Vatican has expressed its condolences to Islam over the deaths of 343 people in a blaze during the haj pilgrimage to the holy city of Mecca, a Vatican official said on Friday.
The official said the message had been sent to "various personalities in the Moslem world" by the secretary of the Vatican's Pontifical Council for Inter-religious dialogue, Cardinal Francis Arinze.

"We pray to Almighty God that the pilgrims who died may find the grace and compassion of the Lord and that those who were injured may receive the comfort and support which they need so much," the official quoted the message as saying.
Tuesday's fire tore through 70,000 tents at the plain of Mena, about 11 km (seven miles) from Mecca in Saudi Arabia, killing 343 people and injuring some 1,300.
Pope John Paul, the leader of the world's Roman Catholics, has frequently called for dialogue with Moslems, noting that the two faiths share many moral and spiritual values.
